title: Review Timing and Military Service Hold Extensions — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
**Review unit ruling.** Under Hardship and Protective Holds, the anchor of a service extension of a Military Service Hold depends on the status review that next falls due after the hold's current end date. Reviews of this tier fall due every review interval of 90 calendar days counted from the hold's start date, and a review falling due on the current end date itself counts as one inside the hold. The tier's review overdue days are 30 calendar days.

- Where that review falls due no more than 30 days after the current end date and every review that has fallen due by today was recorded as continuing the hold, the service extension is counted from the last day of that review's overdue window, adding the days from the current end date to that review's due date plus the 30 review overdue days.
- Where that review falls due within the same period but fewer reviews were recorded as continuing the hold than have fallen due, it is counted from that review's due date, adding the days from the current end date to that due date.
- Otherwise it is counted from the day after the current end date and adds nothing.

A review whose due date is today has fallen due by today. The test compares the number of reviews recorded in the hold's history as continuing the hold with the number of reviews fallen due by today.

## Dated example (hypothetical)

Start date 1 January; reviews fall due on 1 April, 30 June and 28 September. Today is 15 June, so one review (1 April) has fallen due.

| Current end date | Next review after it | Gap | Reviews recorded as continuing | Days added on this ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 29 June | 30 June | 1 day | 1 | 1 plus 30, that is 31 — counted from 30 July |
| 29 June | 30 June | 1 day | 0 | 1 — counted from 30 June |
| 25 May | 30 June | 36 days | any | Nothing — more than 30 days |

## Boundary points

- A next review falling due exactly 30 days after the current end date qualifies; 31 days after does not.
- A current end date that is itself a review due date keeps that review inside the hold; the next one is 90 days later, so nothing is added.
